meta_desc: Class 3 Give and Take worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 12): mental and column methods, checking and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Give means add on; take means take away.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Add or subtract in parts: 465 + 230 = 665 + 30 = 695.
  • Estimate first: 398 + 205 is about 400 + 200 = 600.
  • Check by doing the opposite.

Examples

Example

Riya had ₹500 and spent ₹235. How much is left?

500 − 235

Answer: ₹265

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up digits from the leftLine up the ones.
Adding in a 'how much is left' problemLeft means subtract.

items.q: What is 62 − 27?

items.q: Which shows 356 partitioned into hundreds, tens and ones?
items.e: 356 has 3 hundreds, 5 tens and 6 ones: 300 + 50 + 6. The 5 is in the tens place, so it is worth 50, not 5.

items.q: Which shows 408 partitioned?
items.e: 408 has 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones: 400 + 8. The 0 holds the tens place, so the 8 is 8 ones.

items.q: What is 527 + 300?
items.e: Only the hundreds change. 5 hundreds + 3 hundreds = 8 hundreds. 527 + 300 = 827.

items.e: You can add numbers in any order. 237 + 156 = 393, the same as 156 + 237. 165 and 273 have digits swapped, so they are different numbers.

items.e: Rearrange: add 38 + 62 first to make 100. Then 100 + 145 = 245.

Where does the last jump land?
On a trip in BC, the Singh family drove 276 km on Friday and 358 km on Saturday. How far did they drive in the two days?
items.e: Put the two parts of the trip together, so add. 276 + 358 = 634. Check: 634 − 358 = 276.

items.q: A ferry can carry 600 passengers. 437 passengers are on board. How many more passengers can get on?
items.e: Find how many more fit, so subtract. 600 − 437 = 163. Check: 163 + 437 = 600.

items.q: Om’s chapter book has 304 pages. He has read 128 pages. How many pages are left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 304 − 128 = 176. Check: 176 + 128 = 304.

items.q: The school library has 750 books. 286 books are checked out. How many books are on the shelves?
items.e: Books checked out are taken away, so subtract. 750 − 286 = 464. Check: 464 + 286 = 750.

items.q: Ananya had some hockey cards. She got 135 more for her birthday. Now she has 402 cards. How many cards did she have at the start?
items.e: Work backwards. Take away the 135 that were added: 402 − 135 = 267. Check: 267 + 135 = 402.

items.q: A ferry stopped at Salt Spring Island and 168 passengers got off. Now 279 passengers are on the ferry. How many passengers were on the ferry before the stop?
items.e: Work backwards. Add back the 168 that were taken away: 279 + 168 = 447. Check: 447 − 168 = 279.

items.q: A trail through the cedar trees in Stanley Park is 900 m long. Rohan walked 345 m, rested, then walked 278 m. How many metres are left?
items.e: Step 1, metres walked: 345 + 278 = 623. Step 2, metres left: 900 − 623 = 277.

items.q: A ferry to the Gulf Islands left with 534 passengers. At the first island, 185 passengers got off and 98 passengers got on. How many passengers are on the ferry now?
items.e: Step 1, after the passengers got off: 534 − 185 = 349. Step 2, after the new passengers got on: 349 + 98 = 447.

items.q: In the first hour, 386 people got on the SkyTrain at one station. In the second hour, 127 fewer people got on. How many people got on in the two hours?
items.e: Step 1, the second hour: 386 − 127 = 259. Step 2, both together: 386 + 259 = 645.

items.q: Lakshmi read 236 pages over Spring Break. Siddharth read 148 more pages than Lakshmi. How many pages did they read together?
items.e: Step 1, the second reader’s pages: 236 + 148 = 384. Step 2, both together: 236 + 384 = 620.

items.q: On a road trip, a family drove 268 km on the first day and 345 km on the second day. How far did they drive altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 268 + 345 = 613. Check: 613 − 345 = 268.

items.q: The school library has 476 picture books and 185 chapter books. How many books is that altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 476 + 185 = 661. Check: 661 − 185 = 476.

items.q: The library has 742 books. 158 books are borrowed. How many books are still on the shelves?
items.e: Borrowed books leave the shelves, so subtract. 742 − 158 = 584. Check: 584 + 158 = 742.

items.q: A family is driving 450 km to the beach. They have driven 287 km. How many kilometres are left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 450 − 287 = 163. Check: 163 + 287 = 450.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, Red house scored 312 points and Blue house scored 245 points. How many more points did Red house score?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 312 − 245 = 67. Check: 67 + 245 = 312.

items.q: The school concert has 500 tickets. 263 tickets have been sold. How many tickets are left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 500 − 263 = 237. Check: 237 + 263 = 500.

items.q: A road trip is 703 km long. The family stops for lunch after 285 km. How much further do they have to drive?
items.e: Find the distance left, so subtract. 703 − 285 = 418. Check: 418 + 285 = 703.

items.q: Simran had some points in a maths game. She lost 175 points. Now she has 389 points. How many points did she have at the start?
items.e: Work backwards. Add back the 175 that were lost: 389 + 175 = 564. Check: 564 − 175 = 389.

items.q: The canteen had 512 bottles of water. It sold 168 at recess and 195 at lunch. How many bottles are left?
items.e: Step 1, bottles sold: 168 + 195 = 363. Step 2, bottles left: 512 − 363 = 149.

items.q: The library had 625 books. 248 books were borrowed. Then 136 books came back. How many books are there now?
items.e: Step 1, after borrowing: 625 − 248 = 377. Step 2, after the books came back: 377 + 136 = 513.
